# Jonah Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 340v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JON_002_page_001.jpg

---

**2:1** And-prayed [vayitpallel] Yonah to YHWH his-God from-the-belly [mi-me'ei] of-the-fish.

**2:2** And-he-said: "I-called [qarati] out-of-my-distress [mi-tsarah] to YHWH, and-he-answered-me [vayya'aneni]; from-the-belly [mi-beten] of-Sheol I-cried [shivva'ti], you-heard [shamata] my-voice [qoli]."

**2:3** "And-you-cast-me [vatashlikheini] [into the] deep [metsula], in-the-heart [bi-levav] of-the-seas [yammim], and-the-current [nahar] surrounded-me [yesoveveni]; all your-breakers [mishbarekha] and-your-waves [galekha] over-me passed [avaru]."

**2:4** "And-I said, 'I-am-driven-away [nigrashti] from-before [mi-neged] your-eyes [einekha]; yet [akh] I-will-look-again [osif lehabbeit] toward your-holy [qodshekha] temple [heikhal].'"

**2:5** "The-waters [mayim] encompassed-me [afafuni] to [the] soul [nefesh]; the-deep [tehom] surrounded-me [yesoveveni]; weeds [suf] were-wrapped [chavush] around-my-head [roshi]."

**2:6** "To-the-bases [le-qitsvei] of-the-mountains [harim] I-went-down [yaradeti]; the-earth [ha-arets], her-bars [bericheyha] [were] around-me forever [le-olam]; but-you-brought-up [vata'al] from-the-pit [mi-shachat] my-life [chayyai], O-YHWH my-God [elohai]."

**2:7** "When-fainted [be-hitattef] upon-me my-soul [nafshi], YHWH I-remembered [zakharti]; and-came [vatavo] my-prayer [tefillati] to-you, to your-holy [qodshekha] temple [heikhal]."

**2:8** "Those-who-cling [meshamrim] to-vanities [havlei] of-emptiness [shav], their-loyalty [chasdam] they-forsake [ya'azovu]."

**2:9** "But-I, with-the-voice [be-qol] of-thanksgiving [todah], will-sacrifice [ezbechah] to-you; what I-have-vowed [nadarti] I-will-pay [ashallema]. Salvation [yeshuah] [belongs] to-YHWH."

**2:10** And-spoke [vayyomer] YHWH to-the-fish, and-it-vomited [vayyaqe] Yonah to the-dry-land [ha-yabbashah].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — "from the belly of Sheol":** Jonah's psalm uses the language of the Psalter — compare Psalm 18:5-6, 42:7, 69:1-2. Whether Jonah "actually died" or speaks hyperbolically is debated; the Hebrew places him in Sheol (the realm of the dead) poetically.

**v.5 — "weeds wrapped around my head":** *Suf* ("reeds/seaweed") — the same word as in *Yam Suf* ("Sea of Reeds," i.e., the Red Sea). The echo links Jonah's descent to the Exodus sea-crossing.

**v.8 — "vanities of emptiness":** *Havlei shav* — "vapors of worthlessness." The word *hevel* (vapor/vanity, cf. Ecclesiastes) appears here in construct with *shav* (emptiness/falsehood). Jonah contrasts idol-worship with YHWH-worship.

*— EMET*
